prompt: The Sharpless asymmetric epoxidation uses Ti(OiPr)₄, tBuOOH, and a chiral tartrate (DET) on an allylic alcohol. What determines which enantiomer of epoxide forms?

options.label: The chirality of the DET ligand ((+)-DET vs (−)-DET) — the chiral Ti complex delivers O to a specific face of the alkene.
Reaction temperature — lower T favors one face, higher T the other, via different TS energies.
Solvent polarity — polar solvents stabilize one TS over the other, flipping the facial selectivity.
The configuration of the allylic alcohol's OH stereocenter — the substrate's chirality overrides the catalyst's.

explanation: Sharpless' Nobel-winning method works on allylic alcohols — the OH coordinates to Ti, orienting the substrate so the chiral DET dictates which alkene face gets oxidized. (+)-DET and (−)-DET give opposite enantiomers predictably. If the starting alcohol is racemic/achiral, DET still controls the product chirality.
